started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'll help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

Let me start by asking about your child. **How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over don't qualify

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me continue with the assessment based on your situation. You mentioned you're asking about Alex, who is 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Since Alex is 9 years old (under 16), that's good - children under 16 can qualify for Child Benefit.

Now, **is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, **is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

In other words, is Alex receiving any of these benefits themselves?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about apprenticeships. **Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

If yes, which type? (This matters because certain apprenticeships can disqualify from Child Benefit, while others are approved.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, regarding your residency: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is one of the main ways to meet the residency requirement. There are also other special circumstances that can qualify you (such as having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant abroad), but the simplest path is if you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! You meet the residency requirements. Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Do you live with Alex?** 

(This is the most straightforward way to show responsibility. Alternatively, you could also qualify by contributing to their upkeep or paying maintenance.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You are responsible for Alex since you live together.

Now, an important question: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

(Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! No one else is claiming for Alex. Now I need to check about Alex's living situation.

**Is Alex:**
- In hospital (for an extended stay)?
- In local authority care?
- Being fostered?
- Or living normally with you at home?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex is living normally with you at home. 

One final question: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying for Alex's care or living costs?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Excellent News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex! 🎉**

You've met all the eligibility requirements:

✅ **Alex is 9 years old** (under 16, so qualifies automatically)  
✅ **Alex is not in full-time work** (not working 24+ hours per week)  
✅ **Alex is not receiving benefits** in their own right  
✅ **Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship**  
✅ **You meet UK residency requirements** (you normally live in the UK)  
✅ **You are responsible for Alex** (you live together)  
✅ **No one else is claiming** Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ **Alex lives normally with you** (not in hospital, care, or fostered)  
✅ **The local council is not paying** for Alex's care

---

## **Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Important:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year
5. Payments are made **every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can find more information and start your claim here: [https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
